land.text: northern New South Wales, 'made the Colony of Queensland'; western boundary 141 E until 1862

predecessors.note: Letters Patent signed 6 June 1859; formally separated on proclamation, 10 December 1859 (Colony of Queensland page).

land.text: Queensland, which 'on 1 January 1901 federated to become a state of the Commonwealth of Australia'

successors.note: The State of Queensland is carried by the commonwealth-of-australia dossier from 1 January 1901.

correction.text: Queensland 'formally separated from New South Wales' on 10 December 1859, with its western boundary at 141 E ('longitude 141 E' until 1862)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: modern Queensland less the strip between 138 E and 141 E north of 26 S, about 1.30 M km2 by the gazetteer. The page gives no area, and no southern boundary (the 29 S line is the researcher's reading from the modern border). Torres Strait Islands are below the grid and annexed only in 1872 and 1879.

correction.text: '1862 saw Queensland's western boundary changed from longitude 141 E to 138 E'; the colony then has its modern extent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: modern Queensland, about 1.60 M km2 by the gazetteer, from 13 March 1862 (Territorial evolution of Australia) to federation. The Torres Strait Islands (1872, 1879) are below the grid. No infobox area on the page.

region.text: northern New South Wales: the Colony of Queensland within its 141 E western boundary

ledger.note: 1859: Queensland is separated from New South Wales. 'On 6 June 1859, Queen Victoria signed Letters Patent to form the colony of Queensland'; 'A proclamation was read by George Bowen on 10 December 1859 whereupon Queensland was formally separated from New South Wales.' The page gives no boundary; the shape is the researcher's reading (the modern state with the 141 E western line).

region.text: land north of South Australia and east of 138 degrees east, from the 138 E line to the old 141 E boundary

ledger.note: 1862: Queensland's western boundary moves from 141 E to 138 E (13 March 1862): 'Land north of South Australia and east of 138 degrees east was transferred to Queensland.' The Queensland page: '1862 saw Queensland's western boundary changed from longitude 141 E to 138 E.'

region.text: all islands lying within 60 miles of Queensland: the Torres Strait Islands

ledger.note: 1872: islands near the coast annexed. 'All islands lying within 60 miles (97 km) of Queensland were annexed to the colony' (30 May 1872), 'mainly to cover the Torres Strait Islands'. The islands are below the grid.

region.text: the Torres Strait Islands were specifically annexed to Queensland

ledger.note: 1879: the Torres Strait Islands are specifically annexed to Queensland (21 July 1879). Below the grid.

1901: Queensland federates. 'on 1 January 1901, it federated to become a state of the Commonwealth of Australia' (infobox 'Federation of Australia: 1 January 1901'). The State of Queensland is carried by the commonwealth-of-australia dossier.

wars.name: Kalkadoon raids and Battle Mountain
wars.outcome: 'Raids conducted by the Kalkadoon held settlers out of Western Queensland for ten years until September 1884 when they attacked a force of settlers and native police at Battle Mountain.' No border moved; the Kalkadoon were stateless.
wars.note: The start year 1874 is counted back from the page's 'ten years until September 1884'; the page gives no outcome of Battle Mountain.

certainty.note: The western boundary is a meridian in the letters patent (141 E, moved to 138 E on 13 March 1862) and the Territorial evolution page dates each change. The southern boundary with New South Wales is not described on the pages opened (modern border used). Control on the ground reached the Gulf and Western Queensland only in the 1880s (Kalkadoon war), so the western limits were nominal for years.

sources.title: Australian frontier wars
sources.note: Kalkadoon and Battle Mountain, western Queensland, to September 1884.

sources.title: Colony of Queensland
sources.note: Letters Patent 6 June 1859, proclamation 10 December 1859, 138 E boundary of 1862, capital Brisbane, federation 1901. No boundary text or area.

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. 3 pages used: Colony of Queensland, Territorial evolution of Australia, Australian frontier wars.
Not entered: the 1883 annexation of south-east New Guinea. 'In 1883, Queensland Premier Sir Thomas McIlwraith annexed Papua (later repudiated by British government)' (Queensland page); the Territorial evolution page says Britain 'rejected the claim, then declared it a protectorate' (4 April 1883 and 6 November 1884). The claim never held land, so there is no gain; the protectorate is the British New Guinea dossier (not written in this run) and papua-new-guinea / commonwealth-of-australia. The Queensland page has no infobox area and no boundary text; the pages disagree on the creation date (6 June 1859 letters patent; 10 December 1859 proclamation) and the dossier starts at the proclamation. Border with the Northern Territory block after 1863 is the 138 E line (modern NT/Qld border).
